faq.q: What is the maturity period for Sovereign Gold Bonds?
faq.a: Sovereign Gold Bonds have a fixed maturity period of eight years. However, investors have an option to exit the bond early after the fifth year, on interest payment dates.

faq.q: How is the SGB redemption price calculated?
faq.a: The redemption price of an SGB is based on the simple average of the closing price of 999 purity gold, published by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA) Ltd., for the last three business days preceding the date of redemption.

faq.q: Is the interest earned on SGBs taxable?
faq.a: Yes, the interest income from Sovereign Gold Bonds, paid semi-annually, is taxable. It is added to your total income and taxed as per your applicable income tax slab rate. However, there is no TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) on this interest.

faq.q: Are capital gains on SGBs taxable at maturity?
faq.a: For individual investors, the capital gains arising from the redemption of SGBs after holding them for the full eight-year maturity period are fully exempt from income tax. This is a significant tax benefit.

faq.q: Can I sell my SGBs before maturity?
faq.a: Yes, SGBs are tradable on stock exchanges. You can sell them before maturity, but if sold within three years, gains are short-term taxable. If sold after three years but before eight years, gains are long-term taxable with indexation benefits.

faq.q: What happens if I don't have a demat account for SGBs?
faq.a: If you did not hold your SGBs in a demat account, you would have received a Holding Certificate. Upon maturity, the redemption proceeds will be credited directly to the bank account linked to your SGB application, as per RBI records.
